plain_english: Don't let thoughts like this upset you: "People will think badly of me and I'll be a nobody." If having a bad reputation is truly bad, then you can't be harmed by what someone else does any more than you can be made immoral by them. Is it your job to gain power or get invited to parties? Not at all. So how is this really disgrace? And how are you really a nobody when you should only matter in the things that are actually up to you — the things where you can have real importance?
original_excerpt: Let not such considerations as these distress you: "I shall live in discredit and be nobody anywhere." For if discredit be an evil, you can no more be involved in evil through another than in baseness. Is it any business of yours, then, to get power or to be admitted to an entertainment? By no means. How then, after all, is this discredit? And how it is true that you will be nobody anywhere when you ought to be somebody in those things only which are within your own power, in which you may be of the greatest consequence?

plain_english: "But my friends won't get help." What do you mean by "help"? They won't get money from you, and you won't make them Roman citizens. Who told you that these things are up to you anyway? They're other people's business. How can you give someone what you don't even have yourself? "Well, go get those things so we can benefit too." If I can get them without losing my honor, integrity, and self-respect, show me how and I'll do it. But if you're asking me to sacrifice my character so you can gain something worthless, think about how foolish that is. Besides, what would you rather have — some money or a loyal, honorable friend? Help me build that kind of character instead of asking me to destroy it.
original_excerpt: "But my friends will be unassisted." What do you mean by "unassisted"? They will not have money from you, nor will you make them Roman citizens. Who told you, then, that these are among the things within our own power, and not rather the affairs of others? And who can give to another the things which he himself has not? "Well, but get them, then, that we too may have a share." If I can get them with the preservation of my own honor and fidelity and self-respect, show me the way and I will get them; but if you require me to lose my own proper good, that you may gain what is no good, consider how unreasonable and foolish you are. Besides, which would you rather have, a sum of money or a faithful and honorable friend? Rather assist me, then, to gain this character than require me to do those things by which I may lose it.

plain_english: "But my country won't get any help from me," you say. What kind of help do you mean? Your country won't get fancy buildings or public baths from you? So what? A blacksmith doesn't provide the country with shoes. A shoemaker doesn't provide it with weapons. It's enough if everyone does their own job well. If you gave your country another honest and honorable citizen, wouldn't that be useful? Yes. So you're not useless to your country either. "But what position will I hold in the government?" you ask. Whatever position you can hold while keeping your integrity and honor. If you lose those things by trying to be useful, how can you serve your country once you've become untrustworthy and shameless?
original_excerpt: Well, but my country, say you, as far as depends upon me, will be unassisted. Here, again, what assistance is this you mean? It will not have porticos nor baths of your providing? And what signifies that? Why, neither does a smith provide it with shoes, nor a shoemaker with arms. It is enough if everyone fully performs his own proper business. And were you to supply it with another faithful and honorable citizen, would not he be of use to it? Yes. Therefore neither are you yourself useless to it. "What place, then," say you, "shall I hold in the state?" Whatever you can hold with the preservation of your fidelity and honor. But if, by desiring to be useful to that, you lose these, how can you serve your country when you have become faithless and shameless?
